This suggests the propagation process is either very slow or stalled, preventing active growth.

vision_report.narrative_description: As the Garden Botanical Observer, my meticulous audit of the chronological image sequence reveals a static state for both the Mexican Mint (P2) and the Money Plant cutting (Unmonitored) over the past five days. The Mexican Mint, residing in its black pot with damp soil, consistently displays two small, dark green leaves, exhibiting no discernible growth. Similarly, the Money Plant cutting in its white cup of water maintains a single, turgid, dark green leaf, yet shows no visual signs of root development or new shoot emergence, indicating a stalled propagation. Both specimens appear to be in a state of survival rather than active thriving, suggesting that current environmental conditions, despite consistent lighting, may be sub-optimal for robust growth. A significant event was the complete loss of visual data on T-2 due to extreme darkness. Furthermore, a new, uncatalogued white label or object became visible behind the Money Plant cup from T-1 onwards, representing an unrecorded introduction to the biome.
